research.summary: Two businesses under one roof at 257 Upper Richmond Road West, East Sheen SW14: a working plumbers' merchant trade counter, and a bathroom showroom stocking premium Italian ceramics from GSI via the distributor 34 St John (a single walnut vanity unit and basin on that range lists at £1,085). The registered company is Stephen Wickes Interior Design Limited (10598180), incorporated 2 February 2017, trading as The Plumbing Merchant, and moved into this site in February 2022. Three employees. Shareholders' funds £47,067 at 28 February 2025. Open Mon–Fri 07:00–16:00, Sat 08:00–13:00, closed Sunday. Genuinely well regarded — #1 in the Google map pack, 4.9 stars from 88 reviews, the best of any merchant in the area — but owns none of that presence: no website, an unclaimed and miscategorised Google listing, no bathroom-search visibility anywhere, and a council directory sending customers to the wrong address. Stephen "Steve" Wickes (47, director since 2017) is the buyer and answers the phone himself — his own customer reviews name him directly serving at the counter. Thomas Tennant (68, director since February 2022, lives a five-minute walk away on Sheen Lane) joined with a capital allotment the same week the business moved into this site; reads as a local backer or partner rather than a day-to-day operator.

talkingPoints: Nobody buys a four-grand bathroom because they walked past a shop. They spend a month looking online first, and by the time they've got a shortlist you were never on it.
You're 4.9 from eighty-eight. Screwfix up at 451 is 3.8 from seventeen. You're beating them on every single thing a customer can judge — and they've got the website.
One of the fitters round there is posting finished bathrooms and naming you in the caption. There's nothing to tag. That's free advertising falling straight on the floor.
Google's got you down as a building materials supplier. Not a plumbers' merchant, not a bathroom showroom. I'll get that changed for you either way — it shouldn't be wrong.
You shut at four. Someone sits down after dinner to plan their bathroom — where does that go? Right now, nowhere near you.
notes: REAL RESEARCH — sourced from Companies House, Google, 34 St John and VisitRichmond (Richmond Council), compiled 11 Sep 2026.

Ask for Steve (Stephen Wickes, director since 2017, age 47) — not Mr Wickes, not "the owner". He works the counter himself and his own customer reviews name him directly. There is no gatekeeper — he answers the phone. Thomas Tennant (director since Feb 2022, age 68, lives round the corner on Sheen Lane) is inferred to be a capital partner rather than a day-to-day operator — never pitch him, but take "I'd need to speak to my business partner" seriously here, it's a real second signature, not a brush-off.
Best time to call: Tuesday–Thursday 10:00–11:30, or 15:00–15:45 (the quiet run-up to the 16:00 close). Avoid 07:00–09:00 (trade rush) and lunch. Skip Saturday — closes at 13:00, too tight a window.

Before dialling: have on screen — the Google rating comparison (4.9/88 vs Screwfix's 3.8/17), the 34 St John stockist listing, and the VisitRichmond entry showing the wrong address. Any of the three may need sending within a minute.

Lead with the showroom, never the merchant. Pitching this as "a website for your plumbers' merchant" makes you the eleventh caller this month. The real story — and the only one that gets a meeting — is the bathroom showroom nobody can find.
Never say "you're invisible on Google" — they rank #1 locally for plumbers' merchants. The real gap is the showroom side, and the fact they own none of their online reputation.

Honest odds from the research: roughly 9/10 chance of getting through (three staff, one line, the owner serves the counter himself), 5/10 of booking a meeting (rises to 7/10 if you lead with the showroom angle, drops to 3/10 if you pitch the merchant angle instead), 4/10 of closing overall but 6/10 for the £400 site alone if reached properly. Net worth is a modest £47k, but he demonstrably spends — two capital raises and a premium stock relationship.

Never mention the £75/month operations product or the £50/month booking tool on this call — if it comes up, tell him plainly he doesn't need them yet. The booking tool is a genuinely good fit in a few months once the site exists, not today.

Nine years of trading with no website is a settled preference, not an oversight — the job on this call is to change his mind, not just inform him. The wedge is that his circumstances have changed underneath that: the showroom and the GSI listing are both relatively recent, and the customer for a £1,085 basin behaves nothing like the customer for a compression fitting.

script.opening: Morning — is that {{firstName}}? ... You don't know me, and I'll be straight with you — this is a cold call. Give me thirty seconds, and if it's no use I'll go away. Alright?
script.hook: You're rated 4.9 out of five from eighty-eight people. The Screwfix at 451, same road as you — 3.8 from seventeen. You're miles better and they've got the website, the app, the lot. And the bit that really got me is you're not just a merchant — you've got the GSI range in there, that's proper showroom stock. That's the whole reason I'm ringing.
script.valueStatement: What I do is small. One site: your ranges, photos of the bathrooms you've supplied, your reviews on it, your hours, and a way for someone to ask about a showroom visit at nine o'clock at night when you're shut. That's it — nothing you don't need.
script.demoOffer: Here's what I'd suggest. Separate from all that — two things are just wrong out there. Google's got you filed as a "building materials supplier", not a bathroom showroom, and Richmond Council's own shop-local page has you at the wrong address with a different phone number. I'll get both sorted for you either way, no charge. On top of that, give me till Thursday and I'll build what your actual page would look like — your ranges, your reviews, your name on it. Fifteen minutes on the phone, you look at the real thing, you tell me yes or no.
script.pricing: It's four hundred pounds, once. Nothing monthly. You've got a vanity unit in the showroom for more than double that — if it brings you one bathroom customer in its whole life it's paid for itself twice over.

discovery.question: When someone comes in about a full bathroom — not a plumber, a homeowner — how did they find you?
discovery.why: The key discovery question from the research — sets up the shortlist point directly.
listenFor: "Recommendation" or "they walk past" both hand you the shortlist line straight away

discovery.question: What's the split for you — counter trade versus the showroom?
discovery.why: Confirms which side of the business actually needs the site before you promise the wrong thing.
listenFor: A meaningful showroom share supports leading with that side, not the merchant side

discovery.question: Do the fitters bring their customers in with them, or do they buy for them directly?
discovery.why: Surfaces the fitter-referral relationship without naming the Instagram post yet — a natural lead-in to it.
listenFor: Any mention of fitters recommending him supports the fitter's-Instagram talking point

discovery.question: How much of the day goes on the phone answering "have you got" questions?
discovery.why: Surfaces the operational pain — three staff, one counter, one showroom — in his own words.
listenFor: Any sigh or "more than you'd think" is the value statement written for you

discovery.question: When someone rings at ten past four, what happens?
discovery.why: Makes the 4pm-close problem concrete without you having to state it as an accusation.
listenFor: "Nothing, we're shut" is the exact gap the evening-enquiry angle fills

discovery.question: How many full bathrooms would you do in a year, and what's a decent one worth to you?
discovery.why: The ROI argument, in his own numbers rather than yours — don't react to whatever he says, just note it.
listenFor: Any figure at all makes the £400 comparison trivial to make later

extraObjections.objection: We've done fine without a website.
extraObjections.meaning: Never contradict nine years of results — agree with them completely before making the showroom distinction.
extraObjections.response: Clearly — 4.9 from eighty-eight people says you've done a lot better than fine. I'm not pointing at the counter. I'm pointing at the showroom, because that customer behaves completely differently.
extraObjections.likelyReply: Suppose that's true. / Go on then.
extraObjections.followUp: Move into discovery: ask how a homeowner planning a full bathroom actually found them.
extraObjections.whenToStop: If he's adamant the showroom doesn't need to grow either, accept it — a business that's genuinely happy with where it is isn't a fit.

extraObjections.objection: Our customers are trade, they don't look at websites.
extraObjections.meaning: True of the regulars, not true of the showroom customer he's describing in the same breath.
extraObjections.response: The plumbers don't, you're right — they've got your number in their phone. But the person choosing a thousand-pound basin isn't a plumber. She's been on Houzz every night for a month.
extraObjections.likelyReply: Never thought of it that way. / Still don't see it.
extraObjections.followUp: Ask the showroom discovery question directly if it hasn't come up yet.
extraObjections.whenToStop: If he's genuinely not interested in growing the showroom side, don't push — offer the free Google fix and leave the door open.

extraObjections.objection: I get ten of you a week.
extraObjections.meaning: Fatigue with generic cold callers, not a rejection of the idea. Prove you're not one of them, checkably.
extraObjections.response: I know, and they all open with "you haven't got a website". I opened with the fact that Screwfix up at 451 is rated 3.8 and you're 4.9. Have a look while I'm on the phone — I'll wait.
extraObjections.likelyReply: (He checks, and sees it.) / Alright, fair enough.
extraObjections.followUp: Once he's seen it, move straight into the showroom turn.
extraObjections.whenToStop: Only offer this if you're certain the numbers are current — check before the call, not during it.

extraObjections.objection: How do I know you'll still be around?
extraObjections.meaning: A fair question about risk, not hostility. Answer it straight.
extraObjections.response: Fair question. It's a one-off four hundred, so you're not tied to me monthly, and the site's yours — domain, files, everything. If I disappeared tomorrow any developer could pick it up. That's deliberate.
extraObjections.likelyReply: Okay, that's reasonable. / Still not sure.
extraObjections.followUp: Move to the demo offer — showing the actual page builds more trust than more words will.
extraObjections.whenToStop: If he remains unconvinced after a straight answer, don't over-argue it — offer to send the example anyway.

extraObjections.objection: Who else have you done this for?
extraObjections.meaning: A reference check. Never invent a client — a fabricated reference is fatal if checked.
extraObjections.response: I'll be straight with you — I'm building this up, so you'd be an early one, and that's exactly why you'd get more attention than an agency would give you. Judge me on the work: let me build yours and show you before you decide anything.
extraObjections.likelyReply: Fair enough. / I'd rather see someone else's first.
extraObjections.followUp: Move straight to the demo offer — the work is the reference.
extraObjections.whenToStop: If he insists on seeing existing client work you don't have, be honest that you don't have it yet rather than stretching the truth.

extraObjections.meaning: A comparison on the wrong axis — price and range, where a chain always wins. Move it to trust and knowledge.
extraObjections.response: You can't and you shouldn't. Nobody's writing reviews about how well Screwfix knew their stuff. Eighty-eight people wrote that about you. I just want it visible before someone walks past you to get to 451.
extraObjections.likelyReply: Suppose that's true. / They're just cheaper though.
extraObjections.followUp: Quote a real review theme back if you have one — his own customers naming him personally.
extraObjections.whenToStop: If cost is genuinely the deciding factor for his customers and not service, be honest this may not shift much — don't oversell it.

extraObjections.meaning: Acknowledge the real value in the 34 St John listing before naming its limit.
extraObjections.response: They do, and it's worth having. But someone browsing GSI on 34 St John's site is shopping the brand, not you — and there are other showrooms on that same page. You're one of a list.
extraObjections.followUp: Move to the value statement — a page that's his and only his.
extraObjections.whenToStop: N/A — this should move the conversation forward, not end it.

extraObjections.meaning: A pre-emptive objection to something you were never suggesting. Agree immediately — don't defend a pitch you didn't make.
extraObjections.response: Nor would I. I'm not suggesting you start posting. The fitter's already doing it for you — it just needs somewhere to land.
extraObjections.followUp: Return to the fitter's-Instagram point or the showroom angle immediately.
extraObjections.whenToStop: N/A — should resolve in one line.

extraObjections.objection: What would you even put on it?
extraObjections.meaning: A buying question in disguise — treat it as one, not as scepticism.
extraObjections.response: Your ranges, the GSI stuff, photos of bathrooms you've supplied, your reviews, your hours, and a way for someone to ask about a showroom visit at nine at night. That's it. It doesn't need to be clever.
extraObjections.likelyReply: Right, okay. / Suppose that makes sense.
extraObjections.followUp: Close straight after this — ask for the fifteen minutes.
extraObjections.whenToStop: N/A — this is a green light, keep moving toward the close.

extraObjections.objection: I've got someone at the counter.
extraObjections.meaning: Literally true in the moment, not a brush-off. Believe it and offer a specific, informed time.
extraObjections.response: Understood, I can hear it. Quick one — is it quieter around half three, before you shut? I'll ring then and it'll take four minutes.
extraObjections.likelyReply: Yeah, half three's fine. / Try tomorrow instead.
extraObjections.followUp: Confirm the exact day and time before hanging up — 15:00–15:45 is the known quiet window before his 16:00 close.
extraObjections.whenToStop: N/A — always worth a specific callback time here rather than giving up.

customNodes.theySay: We come up first on Google already, if anything.
customNodes.whatISay: You do — for plumbers' merchants. Try searching for a bathroom showroom in SW14 and see where you come. That's the half of your business that isn't showing up.
customNodes.goal: Agree with the true thing completely, then reveal the specific gap — the showroom, not the merchant.

customNodes.whatISay: It is — there's a fitter round the corner posting your name on Instagram right now. He's doing your marketing for you and there's nothing to link to. That's word of mouth with the volume turned down.
customNodes.goal: Reframe word of mouth as something already happening that has nowhere to land, not something to replace.

customNodes.whatISay: Fair enough, I won't push it. One thing though: Google's got you as a building materials supplier, not a bathroom showroom. I'll get that corrected for you, no charge, no strings. Who should I confirm it to?
customNodes.goal: Trade a genuine, unconditional favour for a name and a way back in — never push past a clear no.

customNodes.whatISay: Of course. Would it help if I built the thing first so you've got something concrete to show him, rather than trying to describe it? Costs you nothing to look.
customNodes.goal: Take this seriously — there genuinely is a second director here, not a brush-off. Make it easy for him to show his partner something real.

customNodes.whatISay: It's four hundred pounds, once — nothing monthly. You've got a vanity unit in the window for more than double that. If it's still not right at four hundred, it's a genuine no and I'll leave it.
customNodes.goal: Name the number and the ROI comparison before he imagines a bigger one.

customNodes.whatISay: No catch and no monthly tie-in. I'm one person, not an agency with an office and account managers, so you're not paying for anyone's overheads. It's yours outright when it's done.
customNodes.goal: A price question dressed as scepticism is still a buying signal — answer it plainly.

customNodes.whatISay: Course. I'll send you the Screwfix comparison — your 4.9 against their 3.8, same road. Worth seeing either way. Best address? And I'll ring you Thursday about half ten once you've had a look.
customNodes.goal: Accept the email request, but attach a specific, useful thing and a named follow-up time.

customNodes.whatISay: I believe you — most of them do nothing. But you didn't have eighty-eight five-star reviews then, or a GSI showroom. The traffic exists now. There's just nowhere for it to land.
customNodes.goal: Separate "websites don't work" from "that website didn't work" using how much has changed since.

customNodes.theySay: I haven't got time to keep it updated.
customNodes.whatISay: Nobody's updating it — that's the point. Your ranges, your hours, your reviews, a way to book a showroom visit. Built once. If you ever want something changed you ring me.
customNodes.goal: Remove the imagined ongoing work entirely.

customNodes.whatISay: No problem. Can I do this — I'll build it, send it over, and put fifteen minutes in for Tuesday. You look at the actual thing rather than imagining it, and if it's still no, you'll never hear from me again.
customNodes.goal: Never accept an open-ended delay — replace it with a specific near date and something concrete to react to.

customNodes.whatISay: Course I can. Is the quiet run-up before you close — around three, half three — any good? I know you're open till four during the week.
customNodes.goal: Offer a specific, informed time rather than a vague "whenever suits", using the known 16:00 close.

customNodes.whatISay: No problem at all. Is the quiet bit before you shut — around half three — any good? Or is there a better day for you?
customNodes.goal: Pin a specific day and time before hanging up, using what's already known about his short trading day.

customNodes.theySay: This isn't Steve — can I help, or take a message?
customNodes.whatISay: No problem — is Steve in today? It's about the Google listing.
customNodes.goal: Stay brief and specific rather than pitching whoever answered — there's almost never a real gatekeeper here, but stay ready for the rare case someone else picks up.
